newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA IRS dispute may impact companies - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA IRS dispute may impact companies - WSJ.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp's dispute with the Internal Revenue Service over its use of stock options could have implications for other firms' pay plans, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
U.S. tax collectors' legal assault on the company for its deductions for executive pay could dampen the enthusiasm for stock options at other companies, the paper said.
At issue is the use of stock options and whether they should be consider 'golden parachutes' that compensate executives when companies change hands, according to the paper.
The Columbia/HCA case suggests the IRS considers that the gains from the cashed-in options should not entirely qualify as taxable excess parachute payments, the paper said.
That could mean higher taxes for companies with huge stock-option plans, the paper said.
